title: prominent done or assumed next
name: Prominent Done or assumed next
rule: Place the control that finishes the transaction (or the assumed next step) at the end of the visual flow; make it prominent and well labeled.

citation.source: Designing Interfaces 3e ch. Doing Things — Prominent Done or Assumed Next Step (Tidwell, Brewer, Valencia)

pass_when: Finish / assumed-next sits at the end of the visual flow, is prominent, and is well labeled.
fail_when: That control is weak, unlabeled, or not at the end of the flow.
overview: The finish or assumed-next control sits at the end of the visual flow, prominent and labeled.
apply_when: Transaction or multi-step flows that end in a clear done or next step.
not_when: Open-ended canvases with no single finish or assumed-next control.
agent_hint: Place a prominent, well-labeled finish or next control at the flow’s end.
description: The control that finishes the transaction—or the assumed next step—belongs at the end of the visual flow, prominent and well labeled. A weak, unlabeled, or mid-flow finish control stalls completion and makes people hunt for how to done. Place it where reading and form fill naturally end, with clear emphasis. Use this on linear commits; freeform canvases without a single done step are a different layout problem.
